evidence: Cic. Fin. 5.42: eōs agnōscunt, ā quibus ēducantur
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: agnōscere is to recognize what one has known before, cognōscere to get to know (see learn, find out). What one knows it by goes with ex: ex frūctū arbor agnōscitur (Vulg. Mt. 12.33, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: know again, recall; more often, go over, review
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to know again, recollect”, especially in Cicero; from the Augustan age on mostly “to look over, review”.

phrases.latin: nam cum in loca aliqua post tempus reversī sumus, nōn ipsa agnōscimus tantum, sed etiam, quae in hīs fēcerīmus, reminīscimur
phrases.english: for when we go back to a place after some time, we not only recognise it but also remember what we did there

phrases.latin: excipiunt plausū pavidōs gaudentque tuentēs Dardanidae, veterumque agnōscunt ōra parentum
phrases.english: the Trojans greet the nervous boys with applause and delight in watching them, and recognise in them the faces of their forebears
